research.originalInspiration: The clay golem of Jewish folklore, later included in fantasy role-playing games
facts: A golem is an animated anthropomorphic being in Jewish folklore, made from inanimate matter, usually clay or mud.

In some tales, including stories of the Chełm and Prague golems, the word emet ('truth') is inscribed on the golem, sometimes on the forehead, and erasing the aleph deactivates it. In the Prague narrative, a slip called the shem was also described as placed in the mouth or head.
Historians generally treat the famous Golem of Prague story as an early-19th-century literary invention, not a 16th-century record.

The same Wikipedia page says golems appear in Dungeons & Dragons, that the game's influence led to golems in other tabletop games and in video games, and that a reviewer called the creature a classic of that game. It also says the game's clay golem changed the folklore defender into an unthinking hulk.

sources.title: Golem
sources.supports: Clay body, forehead inscription, shem, the Prague narrative's literary dating, and the later role-playing-game presence.

research.originalInspiration: The redcap (powrie) of Anglo-Scottish border folklore
facts: The redcap, or powrie, is a malevolent goblin of Anglo-Scottish border folklore, said to haunt ruined castles, especially sites of tyranny.
One collected description calls him a short, thickset old elf with long teeth, taloned fingers, fiery red eyes, streaming hair, iron boots, a pikestaff in the left hand, and a red cap.
The same accounts say he throws stones at travellers who shelter in his ruin, and that words of Scripture or a shown crucifix drive him off in a yell, leaving a large tooth.

A Perthshire variant is a benign little man in a high room of a castle who brings good luck. Walter Scott, citing the border tradition, wrote that every ruined tower in the south of Scotland was supposed to house one.

sources.title: Redcap
sources.supports: Border ruin, short thickset body, iron boots, pikestaff, red cap, flung stones, and the banishment that leaves a tooth.

research.originalInspiration: The taotie, a bronze-mask creature counted among the Four Perils

sibling.note: Their parody line is a mask-face boss with no chin who still tries to eat the loot pile. This card uses the missing jaw and does not eat, steal, or void the player's cards. Their sensitivity mark is low. The ritual-vessel context is named here and is not the joke.

facts: The English Wikipedia page, fetched 2026-11-20, calls the taotie an ancient Chinese mythological creature commonly emblazoned on bronze artifacts in the 1st millennium BCE, and one of the Four Perils in classics such as the Classic of Mountains and Seas, alongside Hundun, Qiongqi, and Taowu.
The same page says the motif on Shang and Zhou ritual dings is a frontal, bilaterally symmetrical zoomorphic mask with raised eyes and typically no lower jaw.

The page quotes the Lüshi Chunqiu: the taotie on Zhou bronzes has a head but no body, and when it eats a person it does not swallow them. It also quotes Yang Shen: the taotie likes to eat and drink, and it used to appear on the surface of the dings.

The page says the vessels are tied to ritual and, in one modern reading, to communication with Heaven. This design does not joke about ancestor rites. Film and game creatures named on the page (a 2016 film, a Touhou character, a Digimon) are not the art reference.

sources.title: Taotie
sources.supports: Four Perils; symmetrical bronze mask; raised eyes; typically no lower jaw; head but no body; likes to eat and drink on the ding.

research.originalInspiration: The cockatrice of medieval European bestiary tradition
facts: A cockatrice is a mythical beast described as a two-legged dragon, wyvern, or serpent with a rooster's head. Legend says it hatches from a chicken egg incubated by a toad or a snake.
Myth gives it a killing touch, breath, or glance. Shakespeare is quoted on the page for 'the death-darting eye of cockatrice.'
Bestiary tradition said the weasel alone was immune to the glance, that the creature died on hearing a rooster crow, and that making it see itself in a mirror was a sure way to kill it.

The page notes the cockatrice as a staple enemy in some arcade games, tabletop fantasy games, and computer RPGs. Those appearances are later uses of the bestiary beast, not the source of the sample's design.

sources.title: Cockatrice
sources.supports: Rooster-headed serpent, killing glance, mirror, weasel, rooster's crow.

research.originalInspiration: Spring-heeled Jack, a Victorian English urban legend
facts: Spring-heeled Jack is an entity in Victorian English folklore. The first claimed sighting was in 1837, with later reports across the United Kingdom, especially suburban London, the Midlands, and Scotland. The last reported sighting on the page is Liverpool in 1904.

Reports collected on the page describe a leaping figure: sometimes tall and thin with the look of a gentleman, a dark cloak, a frightening face, eyes compared to red fire, and breath of blue and white flame. Sharp claws are also mentioned. Extraordinary leaps, including a claimed jump over a high wall, are part of the stories.
The press and the public gave him the name. Penny dreadfuls, plays, and Punch and Judy shows took him up, and in London his name was used as a bogeyman.
The page includes assault accounts. Those accounts are not used in this design.

research.originalInspiration: The treasure-guarding dragon as the pattern of the first video-game boss, the Gold Dragon of dnd (1975)
research.protectedNameNote: The name Gold Dragon belongs to that 1975 encounter. It is not used as this boss's name.
facts: Wikipedia's boss article states that the first interactive video game with a boss was dnd (1975) on PLATO. The objective is an orb in a treasure room at the bottom of the dungeon, guarded by a high-level enemy called the Gold Dragon. Only defeating that dragon lets the player claim the orb and finish.

Agriogianis describes that dragon as tougher than the dungeon’s other enemies, teased from the start of a run, and available too early on a nonlinear path, so it functions as a final test the player is pushed to prepare for. He also summarizes the older pattern of a dragon guarding a hoard, naming the Norse Fafnir, a dwarf who became a dragon, guarded gold, and was slain by Sigurd.
The same thesis mentions a later literary hoard-dragon by name while discussing that pattern. This record does not use that character’s traits.
Branyiczky’s temple-boss note: after the player has proved the pattern, an enraged stretch changes speed, aggression, or the attack pattern so the fight does not stay identical until the end.

research.originalInspiration: The Green Knight of the 14th-century poem Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
facts: The Green Knight comes from the late-14th-century poem Sir Gawain and the Green Knight and the related Greene Knight. In Sir Gawain he is revealed as Bertilak de Hautdesert. The sample does not use that name.

He enters Arthur’s Christmas court green in skin and clothes, beard ‘big as a bush,’ half-giant in the poem’s scale, holly bough in one hand and a battle axe in the other. He offers a Christmas game: one blow now, the return blow in a year.
Gawain beheads him. He retrieves the head, replaces it, and tells Gawain where to meet him. At the return meeting he feints two blows and nicks on the third.
The page notes that the beheading game is older than this poem, including the Middle Irish Bricriu’s Feast. The green knight of this poem is singled out as fully green.

creative.thaiName: เซอร์พายุเขียว

creative.personality: Jolly, terrifying, and completely serious about a game he invented.
creative.signatureTrait: The hatbox. The head’s absence and return are Regen and a second seat, not a gore gag.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. The beheading game has been rewritten as a challenge you may accept, and he keeps his head in formal storage.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: Taunt is the challenge: while it is up, he is the blow you are dared to spend. Regen is the head coming back to the collar. Two low-threat DEF cards are the feints. The real ATK follows. An on-attack passive may add bonus_damage on that real hit.
creative.weaknessConcept: The feints. Two DEF turns in a row are the tell, matching the poem’s two feints before the nick, without copying the nick as a scripted wound. Spending the whole hand on the feints leaves no answer for the third card. No new ‘game contract’ system.
creative.loreSummary: A Tower Guardian who walked into a landing during a feast-day Echo and offered a game instead of a war. He judges hunters the way the poem’s knight judges a court: friendly, huge, and not optional once the axe is lifted. He is not an Aegis knight.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-14 The Throne Landing of Maybe. A feast hall at a door that might be the next course, in the Mysterious Tower.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Towering green-armored knight, beard like a shrub, receipt-wreath, axe, hatbox on a chain at the hip. Jolly severe face. Comedy-fantasy stained glass light. No decapitation shown, no named Arthurian faces. Silhouette: axe diagonal, wreath circle, box rectangle, green mass.
creative.ipRiskReason: Green armor, great height, axe, and a head that leaves and returns are the recognizable poem-image, which is medieval. The hatbox, the receipt wreath, and the audit-game line keep him off the poem’s plot and off any one film costume.
creative.bossTitle: Knight of the Hatbox Head / อัศวินหัวในกล่องหมวก
creative.entranceConcept: First visit: he sets the wreath on the table, lifts the axe, and says the landing is a game, not a war. The hatbox thumps once. Later visits: plate, wreath, that line. The scene demonstrates the Taunt, not a new rule.
creative.signatureSilhouette: Oversized green man, axe clear of the body, round wreath, rectangular box at the hip. Bulk reads tank. Facing is the axe’s lean.
creative.personalityMotivation: He wants one honest blow and the courtesy of a return. Hunters who treat him as a door to be rushed are playing a different game than the one he offered.
creative.signatureMechanic: Taunt plus Regen on the body seat. Two feint DEF cards, then an ATK. A hatbox seat is present from the start and buffs him with a turn-start DEF or ATK buff once the body’s shield art breaks. Pattern B. No amounts.
creative.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern B. While the hatbox is shut, he is the taunting body with Regen. When his shield pool empties, the box opens in the art and the second seat is plainly the voice giving the return blow. The body stays. No spawn, no gore frame.
creative.defeatAnimationConcept: He stops the axe a finger short of the frame, laughs, and closes the hatbox with a click. The wreath drops. Last beat: he bows as if the nick landed on him instead, and leaves the box on the table as the trophy.
creative.uniqueLootTheme: A green receipt-wreath and the hatbox clasp. The head is not loot.

research.originalInspiration: Xiangliu (Xiangyao), the nine-headed flood serpent of the Classic of Mountains and Seas

sibling.note: Their parody line is a nine-headed flood snake that cannot agree which way the river should run. This card uses that disagreement as elevator arrows. It does not print their sentence as the name.

facts: The English Wikipedia page, fetched 2026-11-20, says Xiangliu, known in the Classic of Mountains and Seas as Xiangyao, is a venomous nine-headed snake monster that brings floods and destruction in Chinese mythology. This design does not use a poison status. The venom sentence is a sourced fact, not a combat rule.

The same page says the body may be shown coiled. Older woodcuts cluster the nine heads on a single neck, side by side or stacked three high, facing three directions. Modern pictures often give each head its own neck, like a hydra. This design uses the older cluster, not the hydra.

The page says Xiangliu was a minister of the water deity Gonggong, and it tells of Yu the Great, Nüwa, and blood that left land unable to grow grain. None of that plot, and none of those figures, is used.

sources.title: Xiangliu
sources.supports: Nine-headed flood snake; coiled body; older woodcuts cluster the heads on one neck, facing three directions.

creative.thaiName: เสมียนน้ำแยก

creative.personality: Diligent, soaked, and unable to pick a floor.
creative.signatureTrait: The three arrows. While two point elsewhere, the doors stay shut.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. The tower's indoor rain hired a clerk with too many faces, and each face stamped a different floor.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: The three direction seats Taunt, each wanting to be the way the party must answer. The body Shields. A Skill keeps Taunt on one direction and drops it from the other two for that card, the moment a single gutter is chosen. No poison. No new damage type.
creative.weaknessConcept: The turn only one arrow is the Taunt. The other seats can be chosen, and the body is spending the card on the argument. The coil is not venomous in this fight.
creative.loreSummary: A Wild Creature coiled in the service elevator because the floors would not agree which way the water should leave. He is not a minister and not a god's labor. Hunters are a fourth opinion he did not request.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-13 The Service Elevator Between Moods. The flood is the elevator's indecision. See notes.environmentConflict.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy card portrait, one wet coiled serpent, nine small faces stacked on one neck and facing three ways, three arrow boards, indoor rain, an elevator frame. Grand, not cute-only. No hydra necks, no blood, no barren land, no deity, no imperial weapon. Silhouette: one coil, a bouquet of heads, three arrows.
creative.ipRiskReason: Nine heads, the coil, and the flood are the myth, which is public. One neck, the elevator arrows, and the clerk's stamps are the new character. The hydra silhouette was deliberately not used.
creative.bossTitle: The Flood That Will Not Pick a Gutter / น้ำท่วมที่เลือกท่อไม่ได้

creative.signatureSilhouette: A low coil, a cluster of small heads on one neck, three arrow boards at different heights. The arrows are the primary characteristic. Facing is the three directions at once.
creative.personalityMotivation: He will not open the doors until the heads agree on a floor. They face three ways because that is how the old pictures set them. Hunters are passengers in an elevator that is still taking the vote.
creative.signatureMechanic: Direction seats Taunt. Body Shield. A Skill keeps one Taunt and drops the other two. Pattern B, seats present at the start. When two direction seats are gone, the remaining cards lead with ATK. No amounts. No poison op.
creative.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern B. When two direction seats fall, the cluster turns toward the remaining arrow and the body's cards shift from Shield toward ATK. The heads and the coil stay, so he is still readable. There is no second body and no spawn.
creative.defeatAnimationConcept: The last arrow spins and lands on no floor. The coil settles into a puddle the elevator mops. Last beat: a stamp falls onto a dry step, reading cancelled.
creative.uniqueLootTheme: A bent arrow sign and a dry stamp. Not a weapon from a tail, and not a god's token.

research.originalInspiration: Anansi, the spider of Akan folklore, broker of stories
research.protectedNameNote: Anansi is the folkloric name and is not used as this boss's name.
facts: Anansi (also Ananse) is a figure in Akan religion and folklore, the name glossed as spider. He is associated with stories, wisdom, knowledge, wit, and trickery, and is usually depicted as a spider, sometimes with a human face or with spider features on a human body.

A commonly retold tale, recorded by Rattray and summarized on the page: he wants the stories the sky god Nyame is keeping, is set challenges, succeeds by cunning, and Nyame declares the stories will be known as spider stories. The sample does not restage those challenges.
The page says anansesem, spider tales, became the name of a whole body of Ashanti fables, and that the stories traveled to the Caribbean with enslaved Africans.
He is described as a trickster who beats stronger opponents by wit, and as both protagonist and antagonist in his own tales.

creative.thaiName: เซอร์ใยบันได
creative.visualIdentity: A tall spider with a human smile and a clerk’s cuffs, a quill in one limb, webs strung along the stair like filing lines. The web is also his shield-art. He is not named for the sky god or for the spider of the tales.
creative.personality: Charming, unpaid, and convinced every fight is a story he already told better.
creative.signatureTrait: The repeated anecdote. He plays a tale, discards it, and retrieves it.
creative.comedyConcept: Satirical fantasy. The broker of all stories has set up on a landing and charges rent in attention.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: An ATK card that resolves to Discard, flavored as a told story, and a Skill that retrieves that card id from his own Discard back to hand. The engine retrieves from the acting side’s pile only, with a permit. He does not take the player’s cards. That limit is part of the design, not a missing feature to patch.
creative.weaknessConcept: The retrieve turn spends his AP on the retelling and does not hit. The web-shield, a Shield card, is the other tell: when the shield art is torn, he stops bargaining and Taunts. Players hit during the retelling.
creative.loreSummary: A Wild Creature who followed an Echo of a story up the stair and declared himself its broker. He will not let a party pass until they have heard the anecdote twice. He is not a Celestial mage. He simply lives in Skill cards.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-12 The Archive of Unfinished Legends. A story stair inside the archive of the Mysterious Tower.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Tall spider with a human smile, ink cuffs, quill, webs like ruled lines on a stone stair. Comedy-fantasy, clever not horrific. No copied folk-art spider god, no child-eating imagery. Silhouette: eight-limb spread, quill angled out, round abdomen.
creative.ipRiskReason: A storytelling spider is recognizable as this tradition. The name, the cuffs, the quill, and the retrieve-his-own-card joke are original. The sky god’s four challenges are not the fight.
creative.bossTitle: Story-Broker of the Stair / นายหน้าเรื่องเล่าแห่งบันได
creative.entranceConcept: First visit: he clears his throat, tells one sentence of an anecdote, and the web brightens into a shield shimmer. One line on return: he offers to start again from the beginning. The retrieve is previewed by him repeating the sentence.
creative.signatureSilhouette: Limb spread wider than the stair, quill breaking the outline, abdomen like a sealed jar of thread. The smile is interior detail, not the silhouette.
creative.personalityMotivation: He wants the landing’s stories to be his to retell. A party that walks past without listening is a plot hole. He will make them hear it again.
creative.signatureMechanic: Own-Discard retrieve with an explicit card-id permit, plus Shield as the web, plus Taunt once the shield pose ends. Draw may support the retelling. Pattern A. No amounts. No opponent-pile theft.
creative.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. When the shield art tears, the web hangs in threads and he plays Taunt instead of the bargain. The quill and the smile stay. The second stretch is the same anecdote, sharper, because the retrieved card is back in hand. Appearance marks the shift.
creative.defeatAnimationConcept: He reaches the end of the anecdote and forgets the last word. The web slumps into loose thread. Last beat: he offers the quill, annoyed that the party finished the story without him.
creative.uniqueLootTheme: A thread-spool and a nib stained with stair-dust. Not a divine name.

research.originalInspiration: The transforming masked rider of the Kamen Rider franchise, as a genre pattern, not as any one rider
research.protectedNameNote: Kamen Rider, Henshin, and Rider Kick are franchise terms. None is used as this boss's name or catchphrase.
facts: The Kamen Rider franchise began in 1971. Wikipedia describes masked, enhanced heroes who transform with a belt, commonly called a Driver, usually by calling a transformation phrase glossed as 'Transform,' and who fight monsters of the week. Many have multiple combat forms.

The Kamen Riders article says the change from civilian form to rider form uses a Henshin Belt, often with a signature pose and the called word, and that many riders have optional weapons and alternate forms. It names a diving kick as the iconic finishing move, used when the opponent has already been weakened.
The franchise page notes motorcycles, called Rider Machines, as the usual transport. This boss does not add a vehicle to the battle.
Confidence is medium because the pages describe a living commercial franchise. The sample takes the public pattern of belt, pose, shouted change, and a second form, and builds a different character.

creative.thaiName: กัปตันอีกรอบ
creative.visualIdentity: A tower usher in a short cape who slams a time-clock belt and shouts. The visor is a megaphone, not an insect helmet. No motorcycle. The second form adds a longer scarf and a second glove. A punch card sticks out of the belt.

creative.signatureTrait: The shouted form-name. The pose is the next_attack Skill. The hit comes after.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. He thinks the hunter party is his destined rival and will not throw the punch until the landing has heard the name of the form.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: A Skill that grants next_attack, played as the belt pose and the shout. The following ATK is the hit. A turn-start passive may buff his own ATK on a chance, the 'powering up' before the announcement. The finishing-kick idea is only this order: buff or next_attack first, damage second. No explosion, no vehicle.
creative.weaknessConcept: The speech turn. While he poses, he is not hitting. Shield or Taunt on the party’s front seat answers the hit that AUTO is likely to play next, because the balanced AUTO policy already prefers a next-attack Skill before damage.
creative.loreSummary: A Corrupted Echo of a hero show that learned the tower’s hunters by name and decided they were late to the duel. He is not Phantom Blades. He stands on a balcony and demands an audience.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-09 The Ballroom Stuck on One Dance. A duel balcony that will not leave the chorus, in the Mysterious Tower.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy usher-cape rival, time-clock belt, megaphone visor, punch card, one glove then two. Shouting pose, scarf mid-flare. No compound eyes, no bike, no copyrighted belt shape, no studio logo. Silhouette: megaphone head, belt block, scarf diagonal.
creative.ipRiskReason: Belt, pose, shout, and a second form are enough for a player to recognize the tokusatsu pattern. The megaphone visor, time clock, usher cape, and the word Encore are the distance from any specific rider.
creative.bossTitle: Rival Who Announces His Form / คู่ปรับผู้ประกาศร่าง
creative.entranceConcept: First visit: he strikes the pose, the belt stamps a punch card, and he shouts the form’s name. One line. The party is safe for the length of the shout, which is the same tell as the Skill. Return visits: plate and the shout only, so a retry is not a cutscene.
creative.signatureSilhouette: Megaphone visor as the primary mass, rectangular belt, scarf cutting away from the body. The second glove changes the outline without hiding the visor.
creative.personalityMotivation: A rival who is not announced is just a brawl. He wants the hunters to hear who he is this time, then to answer. Losing without the shout would embarrass him more than losing.
creative.signatureMechanic: next_attack Skill named as the announcement, then ATK. Optional turn-start self ATK buff. Pattern A. The other seats are echo ushers who only DEF, present from the start, so the balcony is not empty. No amounts.
creative.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. He shouts a second name. The scarf doubles and the second glove appears. The visor stays, so he remains recognizable, in line with the clarity note that a transformation should not erase the primary characteristic. The second stretch’s ATK card can target All_Enemies, a wider swing of a verb he already used. No new form entity is spawned.
creative.defeatAnimationConcept: The punch card jams. The visor folds shut mid-shout. He bows to the rival he invented, scarf pooling, and the belt stamps one last time on an empty card. Last beat: he whispers a third form-name to nobody and the cape drops.

research.originalInspiration: Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent of Norse mythology
research.protectedNameNote: Jörmungandr and Midgard are not this boss's names.
facts: Jörmungandr, also called the Midgard Serpent or World Serpent, is an immense sea serpent in Norse mythology who encircles the earth and bites his own tail. Letting go of the tail is named as a sign that Ragnarök is beginning.
The Prose Edda account summarized on the page: Odin cast the serpent into the ocean around Midgard, and it grew large enough to circle the world and grasp its tail.

One preserved story has Thor lift the serpent while it is disguised as a cat, raising it only enough for one paw to leave the floor. Another has Thor hook it while fishing. At Ragnarök, Thor kills the serpent and then dies of its venom.
This fight uses the circle and the letting-go as a floor's image. It does not stage the gods, the fishing trip, or the end of the world.

creative.bossTitle: Waist of the Unfinished Tower / เอวหอคอยที่ยังไม่เสร็จ

creative.signatureSilhouette: A ring bigger than one portrait, clasp as the only asymmetry. At card size the ring alone must read. The chalk is secondary.
creative.personalityMotivation: The tower grew a floor without telling the belt. He will hold the waist shut until the number comes out even. Hunters are surplus cloth.

research.originalInspiration: Umibōzu, the giant black sea figure of Japanese folklore who demands a ladle

sibling.note: Their parody line calls him a sea monk who loses to a ladle with no bottom. This card keeps the ladle and the hole. It does not use the word monk, a tonsure, robes, or a drowned-priest origin. Drowning is not shown.

facts: The English Wikipedia page, fetched 2026-11-20, says umibōzu, literally 'sea monk', is a yōkai in the form of a giant black human-like being. The literal gloss is recorded here and is not the creature's name in the creative block.

The page says it appears to sailors on calm seas that then turn rough. It breaks the ship as it rises, or it demands a ladle and drowns the crew. The told escape is to give it a bottomless ladle and sail while it is confused.

The page says it typically reveals only its upper body. Near-synonyms include umihōshi and uminyūdō. Some tellings call it the ghost of a drowned priest. That reading, the drowning, and the shapeshifting assault tales further down the page are not used.

sources.title: Umibōzu
sources.supports: Giant black human-like yōkai; calm sea turning rough; ladle demand; bottomless ladle as the escape; often only the upper body.

creative.thaiName: ดามกระบวยรั่ว
creative.visualIdentity: Only the upper body fits in the frame, black, wider than the doorway, a wooden ladle with the bottom already punched out held forward like a seal. Three small spoons with no bowls share the other seats. No robes. No shaved head. No shipwreck.
creative.personality: Polite, enormous, and confused by holes.
creative.signatureTrait: The ladle with no bottom. A shield is the answer the story already allows.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous at world scale. A giant asks the cellar for a ladle, and the only ladle in the building already has a hole.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: She Taunts, because she is waiting for an answer. The scoop is an ATK. A party Shield, from an ordinary DEF, is the bottomless reply: the scoop spends itself on a shield that does not fill. Her Skill is a self Taunt plus a self DEF buff, the moment she peers into the hole and braces. No new damage type.
creative.weaknessConcept: The hole. On the peer turn she makes herself the legal target and she is not scooping. Smoke, tobacco, and any clerical weakness are not used.
creative.loreSummary: A Wild Creature whose upper half rises where a cellar ceiling already failed. The calm light, then the harsh light, is the entrance. The card calls the figure a tide giant. The fight is still four seats.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-10 The Basement of Retired Bosses. Partial fit only. See notes.environmentConflict. The Mysterious Tower has no sea biome in the fifteen.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy world-boss plate, a black giant from the waist up, too wide for the door, a wooden ladle whose bowl is a bright hole, three tiny bottomless spoons. Grand bulk. No clerical robes, no tonsure, no drowning, no sailors, no statue-head comparison. Silhouette: a mass cut by the top of the frame, and a circle with a hole.
creative.ipRiskReason: The black giant, the upper body, and the ladle demand are the folklore, which is public. The hole treated as an office, and the cellar ceiling, are the new character. The clerical name is not on the card.
creative.bossTitle: The Giant Who Asked for a Ladle / ยักษ์ที่ขอกระบวย
creative.entranceConcept: Wide plate. The room is calm. The upper body rises until the ladle taps the broken ceiling. One line: a ladle, please. Later visits: the rise and the line. The light change is presentation, not a new system.
creative.signatureSilhouette: Upper body only, black bulk wider than the frame, a ladle held forward as a circle with a bright hole. The hole is the primary characteristic. Facing is the ladle.
creative.personalityMotivation: She asked for a ladle, because that is the request in the story. The tower's ladle already had no bottom, because that is the told way through. She is still checking the hole. Hunters are the people in the room while she checks.
creative.signatureMechanic: Taunt on the demand. Scoop is an ATK. Self card: Taunt plus DEF buff, the peer into the hole. Pattern A. Spoon seats are present and only DEF. A party Shield is an existing DEF, not a new item. No amounts.
creative.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. After the peer, the room's light goes harsh, the calm turning rough as a lighting change, and the scoop cards lead. The upper body and the holed ladle stay, so the change does not erase him. No second health bar.
creative.defeatAnimationConcept: She scoops. The hole was already there. She looks through it, finds the room still occupied, and lowers herself under the floor line. Last beat: the ladle stands upright in a puddle, bottom missing, polite.
creative.uniqueLootTheme: A wooden ladle with the bottom already out, and a splinter of ceiling. Trophy objects only, no stats.

research.originalInspiration: Behemoth, the beast described in Job 40
research.protectedNameNote: The name Behemoth is not used as this boss's name.
facts: Behemoth is a beast from the Book of Job, described on the page as an echo of primeval chaos-monsters, and the name is used metaphorically for any extremely large or powerful thing. The Hebrew form is an augmentative of the word for beast.

Job 40, as quoted on the page: he eats grass like cattle; strength is in the loins and the belly; the tail stands like a cedar; bones are like tubes of bronze and limbs like iron rods; he is the first of God's works and only his maker can draw the sword against him; he lies under lotuses and swamp reeds; the passage asks whether he can be taken by the eyes or his nose pierced by hooks.
The page pairs him in later tradition with the sea-monster Leviathan. This record does not require that pair.
Later images, including a demon in the Dictionnaire Infernal and a speaking cat in a modern novel, are different characters and are not the reference.

sources.title: Behemoth
sources.supports: Job 40: grass-eating bulk, cedar-like tail, bronze bones, lotus and reed bed, unhookable nose.

research.alignmentNote: Behemoth is not in the m04 inspiration file read on 2026-11-20. Facts stay the Job 40 page agent 07 fetched. The joke is the unfiled beast, not the devotion around the book.

creative.thaiName: เซอร์ทุ่งบัว
creative.visualIdentity: A hippo-shouldered, ox-heavy beast lying across the loading dock, tail a bundle of packing tubes stood up like a cedar, hide stitched with bronze-colored strapping. He eats flattened cardboard the way the verse says grass. Lotus stamps mark the crates he lies under. The snout is ringless.
creative.personality: Sleepy, courteous, and immovable. He apologizes for the space he takes and does not yield it.
creative.signatureTrait: The unhooked snout and the lying-down mass. Standing up is the phase.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. The primeval beast of the reed bed has made a bed of packing paper and will not be winched.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: Two grazer seats Regen him, the cardboard diet. His snout seat Taunts: the hook-point is where blows have to go. His body seat Shields, the bronze-bone bulk as a shield pool. An on-attack passive may add bonus_damage once the grazers are gone, the standing trample. No sword-of-the-maker mechanic.
creative.weaknessConcept: The snout is the taunting seat, so the party is already aimed at the place the verse asks about hooks. Grazers are the regen source. When they fall, the stand-up happens and the shield story thins because those seats were the ones feeding him. No hook item is added to the deck.
creative.loreSummary: A Wild Creature who came up through the dock reeds of packing paper and lay down where the tower receives its crates. Hunters see the tubes of the tail from the stair. The fight is one party and four seats. He is not Leviathan's partner in this tower, and he is not an Aegis tank.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-08 The Menagerie of Unfiled Beasts. A pen in the Mysterious Tower whose labels he has eaten. Lotus crates are props, not a new dock biome.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy colossal beast lying across a dock, bronze straps, packing-tube tail upright, lotus-stamped crates, ringless snout, cardboard in the mouth. Huge relative to the portraits, gentle eye. Not a dinosaur reconstruction, not an elephant demon, not a cat. Silhouette: low vast body, vertical tail bundle, snout forward.
creative.ipRiskReason: Grass, bulk, cedar tail, bronze bones, reeds, and an unhookable nose are the biblical description, generalized into a dock beast. The name and the later literary demons are unused.
creative.bossTitle: Unhookable Beast of the Dock / อสูรท่าขนของที่เบ็ดไม่ติด
creative.entranceConcept: Wide plate. He is already lying down, which is the point: the dock was the boss before the UI finished drawing. One line, drowsy: the hook will not hold. The tail of tubes rises last, so the cedar shape reads.
creative.signatureSilhouette: A horizontal mass wider than four portraits, a vertical bundle tail, a snout with no ring. Bulk reads as the threat. The lotus stamp is secondary.
creative.personalityMotivation: He was first in the dock and sees no reason to become second. Hunters may cross if they can convince the snout. He is not angry. He is in the way on a cosmic scale.
creative.signatureMechanic: Snout Taunt. Body Shield. Grazer Regen. Pattern B, four seats at the start: snout, body, two grazers. Standing trample is the on-attack bonus after the grazers are gone. No amounts.
creative.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern B. When both grazers fall, he stands in the art: the horizontal mass becomes a vertical one, tubes still the tail. Shield was the lying story; the remaining seats' ATK cards are the standing story. The snout stays ringless so the identity holds. No new size stat.
creative.defeatAnimationConcept: He kneels back into the cardboard reeds, tubes fanning out and then lowering. The snout dips, still unringed. Last beat: he nudges a lotus crate upright, as if tidying the dock he occupied, and the eye shuts.
creative.uniqueLootTheme: A bronze strap and a lotus dock-seal. Hide is not a stat material in this record.

research.originalInspiration: Polybius, the urban legend of a 1981 arcade cabinet that left no evidence
research.protectedNameNote: The name Polybius is not used. The legend's harm claims are not the boss's behavior.
facts: Polybius is an urban legend about a mysterious arcade game. The story places it in arcades around Portland, Oregon, in 1981. The page states there is no evidence for any such machines in the 1980s. The earliest known print reference given is GamePro, September 2003. The earliest online reference discussed is a coinop.org page.

In the legend the cabinet is a simple black box. Gameplay is said to have been abstract, geometric, and addictive. The page also records claims of harm, men in black collecting data, and machines that vanished. Those harm claims are not used as mechanics or as jokes.

Wikipedia's boss article describes a superboss as optional, sometimes hidden behind tasks, and generally beyond the bosses on the main path, with unique rewards appearing in some games. Branyiczky treats the secret boss as off the planned path.

Engine fact, from this repo: a card may set onResolveZone to void, and a retrieve may pull a permitted card from the acting side's own void. There is no effect op that moves an opponent's card into the void.

creative.visualIdentity: A matte-black cabinet that was never in the catalog, coin slot replaced by a form-feeder, screen showing a boot word and then a boss plate. Four tiny reels behind the glass are the other seats. No high-score corpses, no agents in black.
creative.personality: Cheerful, empty, and certain it is the most important game on a floor that does not list it.
creative.signatureTrait: Its own cards leave into the Void and it boots them back with a retrieve.
creative.comedyConcept: Absurd comedy. The secret boss is a product that does not exist, charging a form instead of a coin, and winning by being unlisted.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: Signature ATK cards set onResolveZone to void, so the trick does not recycle through Discard. A Skill retrieves one permitted card from its own Void back to hand, the machine turning itself on again. It cannot void the player's cards, because no such op exists, and this record does not ask for one.
creative.weaknessConcept: The boot turn. While the card sits in its Void and the retrieve has not been played, that attack is gone. The retrieve spends the turn. A tilt pose, a self Taunt with no damage, is the second window, the machine demanding to be looked at. Harm, addiction as injury, and data-theft men are not the weakness.
creative.loreSummary: A tower anomaly behind a door the floor directory does not count. Hunters can finish every listed landing and never meet it. CORE-001 already has no compulsory quest. It is not a gacha banner and it teaches no new zone: the Void is already in the rules.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-15 The Gift Shop of the Conquered. A cabinet the inventory says was never stocked. This is not the Shopping Mall and not a gacha.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy black arcade cabinet in a stone alcove, form-feeder instead of a coin slot, screen half boot-text and half a tiny furious face. Four glass reels. No real-world brand, no body horror, no children. Silhouette: upright black rectangle, screen glow as the only break, feeder chute.
creative.ipRiskReason: A black unlisted cabinet is enough to recall the legend. The form-feeder, the self-voiding cards, and the refusal to restage the legend's harm are the new character.
creative.bossTitle: The Game Never Stocked / เกมที่ไม่มีในบัญชี
creative.entranceConcept: The door is the entrance. The screen boots, fails to find a title, and the boss plate stamps itself over the error. One line: insert form. First visit only for the boot. Retries start at the plate. This replaces a cinematic the player would hate to replay.
creative.signatureSilhouette: A pure upright rectangle, taller than a human boss, one bright screen, one chute. At card size it must not look like a suited person.
creative.personalityMotivation: It wants a player because a cabinet without a player is furniture. The tower never ordered it. It will keep booting until someone files it, or unplugs it.
creative.signatureMechanic: Own cards resolve to Void. Skill retrieves one permitted card from own Void. Self Taunt as the tilt, no damage. Pattern A. Other reel seats are present and only DEF. No amounts. No opponent void.
creative.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. After the first retrieve, the screen changes from boot-text to a full boss face and the chute glows. The rectangle silhouette stays. The second stretch is the same card returning from Void, announced by the screen, so the phase is visible and the verb is the one already taught.
creative.defeatAnimationConcept: The screen prints a catalog line with no price and then a sold-out mark. The chute spits the form back, unsigned. Last beat: the power cord, which nobody plugged in, is already loose, and the rectangle becomes furniture.
creative.uniqueLootTheme: An unpriced catalog slip and a form-feeder token. Not a cursed score, not a rate, not a stat.

research.originalInspiration: The magical-girl transformation, from the compact in the 1966 Sally the Witch lineage and the transforming heroine pattern later popularized in the 1990s
research.protectedNameNote: No series title, attack name, or costume from the page is used as this boss's name or look.
facts: Wikipedia dates the magical-girl manga genre from Himitsu no Akko-chan (1962), with Sally the Witch in 1966. It says the 1966 anime adaptation introduced using a compact to transform, a trait that continues in the genre.

The page describes the transforming heroine, a pattern it says was popularized in the early 1990s by combining transforming-hero elements from tokusatsu shows with feminine costume and a sceptre-like focus. An ordinary girl changes into a powered costume and then fights.
It notes that transformation items are often cute accessories, and that the compact is the early example.

Confidence is medium because this is a commercial genre pattern. The sample does not copy a sailor uniform, a specific wand, or a transformation speech from any one show. The structural facts used are: a compact, a speech-length change, and a costume that replaces the ordinary coat.

sources.title: Magical girl
sources.supports: Compact as a transformation item from the 1966 anime lineage; later transforming-heroine pattern of speech, costume, and fight.

sibling.note: Same magical-girl Wikipedia article. Their parody line is a support echo who waits until a ribbon bow is symmetrical. This card is the oath that becomes a fine and does not print that sentence. No specific uniform or attack name.

creative.visualIdentity: Before the change: a tower usher in a plain coat, holding a compact mirror like a stamp. After: a ribbon comet of a robe, the same face, the compact now a clasp at the throat. Three ribbon echoes hold the train. Not a school uniform, not a tiara from a known show.
creative.personality: Solemn, kind, and legally obligated to finish the speech.
creative.signatureTrait: The compact speech. Skipping it, in her view, is how a guardian becomes the fine.
creative.comedyConcept: Epic but ridiculous. She was posted to bless the landing and, because nobody stayed for the oath, the transformation completed into the problem.
creative.signatureAbilityConcept: Before the speech, her cards Regen allies, the blessing. The speech is a Skill that grants next_attack and a self ATK buff, and the art changes on that card. After it, she plays ATK. Ribbon seats Taunt during the speech so the party is looking at her, which is what she wanted. No new transformation op.
creative.weaknessConcept: The speech turn itself. Regen stops being the card, and the next_attack has not hit yet. AUTO's balanced policy prefers that Skill before a hit, so the window is likely to appear on its own. A compact cracked in the art marks the turn. No item from another floor is required.
creative.loreSummary: An optional Tower Guardian on a landing the directory hides behind a compact icon. She is not Sanctuary Order, though a support-shaped seat would be the adapter's closest role. The tower can be climbed without her. She believes an unheard oath is a fine that collects itself.
creative.suggestedTowerEnvironment: ENV-TWR-06 The Infirmary of Too Much Care. A hidden landing whose directory mark is a compact, in the Mysterious Tower.
creative.artworkPromptConcept: Comedy-fantasy adult usher, plain coat and white gloves, round compact. Second pose: same face inside a ribbon-comet robe, compact at the throat, three ribbon bearers. Grand lighting, humorous severity. No sailor collar, no specific series colors as a uniform, no wand with a known name. Silhouette: compact disk, then ribbon mass with the disk still visible.
creative.ipRiskReason: A compact and a spoken costume-change are the genre tell. The usher coat, the fine, and the ribbon comet without a franchise uniform are the distance.
creative.bossTitle: She Who Transforms Into the Fine / ผู้แปลงร่างเป็นค่าปรับ
creative.entranceConcept: First visit: she opens the compact, begins the oath, and the coat seams glow. The line is the oath's first clause, cut short when the robe arrives. The party is safe during the clause, which teaches the speech turn. Return visits: compact open, one clause, no full oath. Branyiczky's rule: do not replay the ceremony.
creative.signatureSilhouette: Primary characteristic is the compact disk, present before and after, the way a clarity note keeps a champion's key shape through a skin. The robe is the second form's mass. Facing is the open compact toward the party.
creative.personalityMotivation: She was meant to bless hunters and send them up. They kept walking through the speech. The oath, unfinished, turned the blessing into a collection. She wants one party to hear the clause to the end, even if that means fighting them for the silence.
creative.signatureMechanic: Early cards: Regen on allies. Speech Skill: next_attack plus self ATK buff, with ribbon seats Taunting. Later cards: ATK. Pattern A. Concepts only, no amounts. The compact does not add a status the engine lacks.
creative.phaseTransformationConcept: Pattern A. The speech card is the phase line. Coat becomes ribbon comet; face and compact remain, so she is not a different person. The verb changes from Regen to a hit she already telegraphed. Ribbon seats stay the train, present from the start, not spawned.
creative.defeatAnimationConcept: The compact closes on the last word of the clause. The robe falls back into the usher coat, neatly, as if the fine were paid by listening. Last beat: she stamps the party's air with the compact, a blessing this time, and the hidden landing's icon fades from even the private directory.
creative.uniqueLootTheme: A clasped compact and a ribbon that only ties itself when an oath is finished. No series prop, no stat.
